saints.name: Our Lady of Mount Carmel
saints.title: Commemoration of the Blessed Virgin Mary
saints.shortBlurb: The Blessed Virgin honored as patroness of the Carmelite Order and mother of the Brown Scapular…
biography: Mount Carmel — in Hebrew Karm-El, the 'garden' or 'vineyard of God' — is the headland where Elijah confounded the prophets of Baal and saw the little cloud rise from the sea, an image long read as a figure of Mary. There, in the late twelfth century, hermits of the crusader states made their home.

These hermits, founders of the Carmelite Order, built among their cells a chapel to the Blessed Virgin and honored her as the 'Lady of the place'; early in the thirteenth century St. Albert, Patriarch of Jerusalem, gave them a rule. Driven west by the Saracen advance, they carried her name into Europe.

The feast began in fourteenth-century England as the order's thanksgiving to its patroness; fixed on 16 July, it was extended to the whole Latin Church by Benedict XIII in 1726. Its medieval sequence, the Flos Carmeli, the 'Flower of Carmel,' still honors her.

The day is bound to the Brown Scapular: a tradition first attested in the later fourteenth century says Our Lady gave the little habit to the Carmelite Simon Stock, promising that whoever dies wearing it shall not suffer everlasting fire; those who wear it claim her as patroness.
saints.knownFor: Patronage of Carmel and the devotion of the Brown Scapular.
patronage: those who wear the Brown Scapular

sources.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), “Our Lady of Mount Carmel”
